1.note: חר"י חזן, "the sage R. Y. Ḥazan": R. Jacob le-Vet Ḥazan, who travelled with R. Yom Tov Algazi as emissary of Jerusalem; so the notes of A. Freimann, Ma'agal Tov ha-Shalem (Berlin–Jerusalem 1921–34).

2.note: The date does not agree with itself. 3 Nisan 5535 was Monday 3 April 1775, in the week of Metzora. 3 Sivan 5535 was Thursday 1 June 1775, in the week of Bemidbar, so "Nisan" is probably a misprint for "Sivan". Dates from the Hebrew calendar (Hebcal, diaspora readings).

3.note: Literally "to pass them": perhaps through the customs or the health officers, as with the clothes at Venice below. Sense uncertain.

4.note: So printed: "knowledge and patience and expenses". Perhaps the means to bear the expenses. Sense uncertain.

5.note: An abbreviated name, printed thus (checked on the scan). Educated guess: מוהריט"א = "our teacher R. Yom Tov A[lgazi]", the same man who came to Livorno in Shevat 1775 (paragraph 13) and was back in Jerusalem by 1776; the initials fit, and he is named with the same title. Not certain.

7.note: איזבירו is Italian sbirro, a police officer. לבלם ("to stop, hold back") is unclear; read as a search or seizure of the clothes, perhaps for the health office or the customs.

8.note: The parts of the date do not agree. 28 Elul 5536 was Thursday 12 September 1776. The Sunday of the week before Rosh ha-Shanah (named for Ha'azinu, the next reading) was 8 September (24 Elul); the Sunday of the week of Ha'azinu itself was 15 September, the second day of Rosh ha-Shanah. The first letters of the date could also be read כ"א (21 Elul, Thursday 5 September).

9.note: So printed; probably for הח' השלם, "the accomplished sage".

10.note: Unclear word; read as "partitions" (מחיצות), perhaps hedges.

12.note: The second column in the Piazzetta carries St Theodore, the old patron of Venice. The Ḥida gives the story he was told; "the fear of Genoa" is literal.
